issue.body:
The one-shot ragged-all-to-all crashes when the clique has more than 32 devices. We see this on GB200 NVL72 (16 nodes × 4 GPUs, one 64-device clique, one process per GPU). The first execution fails on many ranks at once with `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS`. The crash is deterministic (5/5 training runs). The identical program at 16 ranks runs correctly.

## Minimal repro

The repro needs more than 32 GPUs in one NVLink domain. Smaller domains (for example, B200 NVL8) never reach the affected path. Verified on GB200 NVL72 with stock nightly `0.11.1.dev20260811`: 64 devices crash, 16 devices print `ok`.

```python
# One process per GPU (or per node) across a >32-GPU NVLink domain.
#   export XLA_FLAGS='--xla_gpu_ragged_all_to_all_mode=symmetric'
#   python repro.py <coordinator_host:port> <num_processes> <process_id>
# If the one-shot declines (INVALID_ARGUMENT: "fallback to NCCL is not allowed"),
# add --xla_gpu_unsupported_override_fast_interconnect_slice_size=<total GPUs>.
import sys
import jax, jax.numpy as jnp, numpy as np
from jax.sharding import Mesh, PartitionSpec as P

coord, n_proc, pid = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), int(sys.argv[3])
jax.distributed.initialize(coord, num_processes=n_proc, process_id=pid)
n = jax.device_count()
mesh = Mesh(np.array(jax.devices()), ("x",))

def f(operand, output):
    i = jax.lax.axis_index("x").astype(jnp.int64)
    in_off = jnp.arange(n, dtype=jnp.int64)       # local row j goes to peer j
    sizes = jnp.ones(n, dtype=jnp.int64)
    out_off = jnp.full((n,), i, dtype=jnp.int64)  # receiver row = sender index
    recv = jnp.ones(n, dtype=jnp.int64)
    return jax.lax.ragged_all_to_all(operand, output, in_off, sizes, out_off, recv, axis_name="x")

operand = jnp.arange(n * n * 4, dtype=jnp.bfloat16).reshape(n * n, 4)
output = jnp.zeros((n * n, 4), dtype=jnp.bfloat16)
result = jax.jit(jax.shard_map(f, mesh=mesh, in_specs=(P("x"), P("x")), out_specs=P("x")))(operand, output)
jax.block_until_ready(result)
print(f"process {jax.process_index()}: ok ({n} devices)", flush=True)
```

## Root cause hypothesis

The one-shot barrier supports at most [`kMaxPeers = 32`](https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/3a767ceae167531faac975b92aa6d1df1a7bcedd/xla/stream_executor/gpu/multi_gpu_barrier_kernel.h#L52) peers ([both kernel variants](https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/3a767ceae167531faac975b92aa6d1df1a7bcedd/xla/stream_executor/gpu/multi_gpu_barrier_kernel.h#L69)). [`LaunchMultiGpuBarrier`](https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/3a767ceae167531faac975b92aa6d1df1a7bcedd/xla/backends/gpu/runtime/collective_kernel_api.cc#L88) rejects larger cliques with a [`TF_RET_CHECK`](https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/3a767ceae167531faac975b92aa6d1df1a7bcedd/xla/backends/gpu/runtime/collective_kernel_api.cc#L94-L95). The NCCL-window variant [`LaunchMultiGpuBarrierWithNccl`](https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/3a767ceae167531faac975b92aa6d1df1a7bcedd/xla/backends/gpu/runtime/collective_kernel_api.cc#L120) has no such check. It launches with a [32-slot signal layout](https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/3a767ceae167531faac975b92aa6d1df1a7bcedd/xla/backends/gpu/runtime/collective_kernel_api.cc#L137) and passes `num_devices = 64` to the device kernel. Ranks then index signal slots past the 32-slot region of the symmetric window. The result is device memory corruption instead of a clean error.

The [thunk selects this path](https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/3a767ceae167531faac975b92aa6d1df1a7bcedd/xla/backends/gpu/runtime/ragged_all_to_all_thunk.cc#L1008-L1015) whenever `lsa_size == num_devices`. That condition is always true for a rack-wide NVL72 clique.

## Fix validation

We rebuilt `jax-cuda13-pjrt` at the dev20260811 pins with one change: `kMaxPeers = 32 → 128`. The kernel is fully parameterized on the constant. The crash at 64 ranks is gone. A 25-step expert-parallel MoE training benchmark (384 experts, top-8 routing) completes 25/25 steps. At 16 ranks, the patched wheel matches stock throughput (22.48% vs 22.46% MFU).

## Environment

- GB200 NVL72, 16 nodes × 4 GPUs, one process per GPU, CUDA 13
- jax/jaxlib/plugin/pjrt `0.11.1.dev20260811` (stock nightly), NCCL 2.30.7
- Crash analyzed at jax `fe0f1193` / xla `3a767cea`; fix validated on a rebuild at jax `8d1be7d7` / xla `60f8069e`
- Related: [#47146](https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/47146) (ragged-all-to-all device-kernel peer-access gate on the same topology)

issue.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

Ragged EP now trains the exact four-node proxy with zero routing drops and reaches 19.63% mean MFU, up from 11.28%. Two independent problems caused the original result: XLA's latency-hiding schedule corrupted the first backward at larger expert banks, and the one-shot ragged transfer launched only one 128-thread block per peer. Disabling latency hiding and splitting each peer slice into 32 updates makes the transport finite and raises its grid from 16 to 512 blocks. Reusing the existing QuACK/CuTe SM100 grouped GEMMs removes most of the remaining local expert-compute gap.

The final command-buffer arm completed cleanly but regressed the proxy to 19.34% MFU. Exact-shape weight-gradient tile sweeps bound the remaining packaged kernel gain below the target. The selected configuration therefore remains just under 20%; a full-rack validation is the remaining production gate, not another obvious NCCL or XLA flag.

### Helpful links

- [Implementation PR #8081](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8081)
- [Incident record](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/101)
- [Original XProf](https://iris.oa.dev/proxy/xprof/open?uri=s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Ftmp%2Fttl%3D30d%2Fxprof%2Fra2a-s25-exact-ep16-e48-profile-20260810)
- [Split-32 XProf](https://iris.oa.dev/proxy/xprof/open?uri=s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Ftmp%2Fttl%3D30d%2Fxprof%2Fra2a-s29-exact-ep16-e48-split32-profile-20260810)
- [CuTe XProf](https://iris.oa.dev/proxy/xprof/open?uri=s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Ftmp%2Fttl%3D30d%2Fxprof%2Fra2a-s34-exact-ep16-e48-split32-cute-profile-20260810)
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Experiment contract

The exact proxy used d6144/L48, 48 routed experts of width 6272, latent width 3072, top-4 routing, capacity 1.33, EP16, and 1,048,576 tokens per step across four GB200 nodes. Each node ran four one-device JAX processes. Scored jobs occupied one rack and NVLink domain. PGLE, gradient watch, eval, periodic metric steps, profiling, and checkpoints were disabled for timing runs. Results use steps 5-24.

The proxy matches the one-rack EP64 hero's per-GPU work: both route 65,536 tokens and hold three experts per GPU. EP64 raises global batch and device count together, so it does not enlarge local expert GEMMs or imply a larger-run uplift. A full-rack validation is still required before changing the hero run.

## Results

| Arm | Step time | Tokens/s | MFU | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| One update/peer, latency hiding on, overlap 4 | 33.7040 s | 31,112 | 11.3220% | Finite exact baseline |
| One update/peer, latency hiding off, overlap 1 | 33.8187 s | 31,006 | 11.2834% | Safe flags neutral at exact shape |
| 32 updates/peer, Pallas expert compute | 21.1090 s | 49,675 | 18.0770% | 60.21% throughput gain |
| Split-32, 4 MiB NCCL buffer | 21.1213 s | 49,647 | 18.0669% | Neutral |
| Split-32, QuACK/CuTe expert compute | 19.4429 s | 53,940 | 19.6291% | Best stable configuration |
| Split-32, CuTe, command buffers on | 19.7338 s | 53,137 | 19.3369% | 1.49% throughput regression |

Every completed exact arm had finite loss and zero dropped assignments, dropped-token fraction, or router overflow.

## Findings

- XLA latency hiding corrupts the first backward pass at larger expert banks. Disabling `--xla_gpu_enable_latency_hiding_scheduler` restores finite training. The ragged runtime also uses collective overlap limit 1; this improved the small EP8/E96 proxy but was neutral on exact EP16/E48.
- The original ragged kernel used `grid=(16,1,1)` and consumed 13.82 seconds per step. Split-32 selects XLA's existing multi-update path, uses `grid=(16,1,32)`, and reduces the transfer to 0.78 seconds per step without changing capacity or tensor layout.
- After split-32, the gap to fixed all-to-all was expert compute. Ragged `moe_up_down` took 8.965 seconds per step versus 4.502 seconds for fixed; ragged communication was 0.886 seconds faster. The CuTe flavor keeps ragged dispatch/combine and runs the activation-path grouped GEMMs through QuACK/CuTe, reducing clean step time by another 7.89%.
- CuTe XProf measures 2.084 seconds per step in the two retained Pallas weight-gradient contractions. Exact one-GB200 sweeps covered 64/128/256 output tiles, K16/K32/K64, two/four pipeline stages, and four/eight warps. The only win was 7.54% on `dw13`; `dw2` retained its original tile. Combining the measured ceiling predicts 19.74% MFU, so it does not justify a four-node arm by itself.
- The trace already contains `ncclSymkDevKernel_AllGather_STMC`, so NCCL automatically selected its NVLS multicast path for the largest all-gathers. Forcing NVLS or SHARP cannot accelerate the custom ragged peer-write kernel. Increasing `NCCL_BUFFSIZE` from 1 MiB to 4 MiB was neutral.
- The XLA `ragged_dot_general` alternative OOMed before step zero on a single 159.32 GiB allocation. The generic symmetric put/signal backend failed with `ncclPutSignal: srcWinHost is not in a valid symmetric window`; the pinned GXL backend is unimplemented.
- Process-per-GPU needs the hero host-memory reservation. A 256 GiB four-node reservation OOM-killed a worker; 850 GiB per node completed. Auto-PGLE is not usable in this topology because four CUPTI sessions on one node collide. The separate stale retry-coordinator bug was fixed in [#8079](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8079).

## Decision

Use one process per GPU, 850 GiB of host memory per node, latency hiding disabled, collective overlap limit 1, 32 logical updates per peer, and the QuACK/CuTe ragged expert backend. Keep PGLE and periodic diagnostic work off for timing. Preserve one update per peer as the general library default and select 32 explicitly in this hero configuration until other shapes are profiled.

Keep `FUSION,CUSTOM_CALL` command buffers disabled. They completed without the historical B200 teardown failure but increased mean step time by 1.50%. Even stacking the independently measured `dw13` tile gain perfectly with that arm predicts about 19.45% MFU, so no combined four-node treatment is justified.

The conventional NCCL, transfer-splitting, packaged grouped-matmul, and bounded Pallas tile arms are exhausted for this proxy. A full one-rack EP64 run should validate the selected configuration but is not expected to improve per-GPU MFU merely through scale.

## Artifacts

- [Experiment logbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/hero-run-why-can-t-we-ragged-all/.agents/logbooks/ragged-ep64.md)
- [Split-32 W&B run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/ra2a-s28-exact-ep16-e48-split32-perf-20260810)
- [CuTe W&B run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/ra2a-s33-exact-ep16-e48-split32-cute-perf-20260810)
- [Command-buffer W&B run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/ra2a-s37-exact-ep16-e48-split32-cute-command-buffers-20260810)
- Weight-gradient benchmark: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/benchmarks/ragged-weight-grad-gb200/2026.08.10.38/results.json`
- [PR #8013](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8013)

issue.body:
Every ragged-class EP64 hero run on the current tree dies at the first training step with `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` inside the transport, followed by `ncclCommWindowDeregister ... unhandled cuda error` and a cudaFreeAsync failure cascade. Both `--flavor ep-ragged` (stock levanter backend) and the new `ep-marin` flavor fail identically; `--flavor ep` (fixed_all_to_all) trains normally. The failure survives every configuration change tried: latency-hiding scheduler on/off, collective overlap 4/1, capacity factor 1.33/1.1, `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION` 0.75/0.80 (peak stays 139.74 GiB, 7.7 GiB under the raised limit — this is not an OOM), and both process topologies (1 process/node and 1 process/GPU).

The lock advanced `nvidia-nccl-cu13` from 2.28.9 to 2.30.7 in the 2026-08 native-package bumps (#8179/#8004 window). The last passing ragged EP64 run (MHEP-001, 2026-08-01, snapshot `b0d20062a`) ran 2.28.9. Single-tray runs at identical per-device shapes do not reproduce (EP4 single-process and EP4 with 4 processes over NCCL P2P both pass 3 fwd+bwd steps at T=65536), so the trigger needs the internode MNNVL/NCCL-window path. Note also the cu12/cu13 wheel path collision (both ship `nvidia/nccl/lib/libnccl.so.2`, last-write-wins), so which library actually loads depends on install order.

Reproduce:
1. On current main, `python -m experiments.grug.moe_hero_ep.launch --run-id <id> --dp-racks 1 --num-steps 25 --flavor ep-ragged --version <v> --run` (as an Iris coordinator job on cw-us-east-08a).
2. Watch the training gang die ~1 minute after compile with the illegal-address cascade; `ncclCommWindowDeregister` failures appear in the teardown.

Expected: the run completes 25 steps, as MHEP-001 did on 2026-08-01 at NCCL 2.28.9.

Branch `marin-ep` pins `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.28.9` via override-dependencies as a candidate fix; a confirmation run (`mep-m8-marin-nccl-25-20260815`) is queued behind cluster capacity. Related: #8077 / PR #8081 (ragged EP stabilization; the EP16 4-node proxy there presumably predates or avoids the bump), #8311 (marin_ep experiment).

## Summary

This campaign tested whether the ragged EP64 all-to-all path could match the fixed-transport hero throughput target while keeping trained-router drops below 2% at the full 8/384 hero shape on one NVL72 rack. The drop criterion is met with large margin: the real-LR drop-trajectory run averaged 0.107% drops over steps 250-299 at cf 1.15. Throughput improved from the initial 20.20% MFU / 223k tok/s configuration to a 21.82% MFU / 241k tok/s frontier after QuACK GEMM scheduling work, with zero drops and bit-identical loss across the tuning arms. The issue's current conclusion is that the in-scope configuration and compute-tuning levers are exhausted: split counts, store width, symmetric buffers, fused device kernel, command buffers, HBM optimizer residency, GEMM tile/cluster/persistence, backward mask removal, and overlap-limit changes do not close the remaining gap. Reaching the original ~25% / ~300k tok/s target now depends on a faster structural transport path, tracked separately in marin-ep, rather than more launch-flag tuning here.

### Helpful links
- Prior ragged EP64 crash/fix campaign: #8077
- Capacity/drop analysis: #8062
- Upstream ragged all-to-all gate: https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/47283

- Final in-scope lever closure: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8317#issuecomment-5309167198

## TL;DR

Campaign start. The ragged all-to-all hero (E384, top-8, i3072, EP64 on one NVL72 rack) runs at 20.20% MFU / 223k tokens/s (`ra2a-mw-g17`, cf 1.00, LR≈0 harness). The goal is throughput comparable to the fixed-transport `moe_hero_ep` template (~25% MFU, ~300k tokens/s per rack) while holding steady-state trained-router drops under 2%.

## Description

#8077 root-caused and fixed the EP64 one-shot crash (openxla/xla#47283, kMaxPeers rebuild wheel) and validated the first ragged EP64 hero run. The ragged transport pools receiver capacity per device, so it drops far less than `fixed_all_to_all` at the same capacity factor: at cf 1.1–1.2 the trained-regime drop rate measures ≤0.05% (analytical replay of #8062 histograms; empirical r02 at EP16), versus ~4% for the fixed template at cf 1.30–1.33. Reference points at hero scale on one rack: fixed transport at iso-active-compute (`mhep-baseline-e192k4-i6144-cf133-fp32-20260814-c`) reaches 23.6% MFU / 251k tokens/s at ~3.9% drops; the half-active-compute reference (`mhep-baseline-e192k4-cf133-fp32-20260814-b`, i3072) reaches 25.3% / 346k.

Reach ~25% MFU / ~300k tokens/s at the full hero shape (d6144/L48, E384, top-8, i3072, latent 3072, batch 1024) on one NVL72 rack with the ragged transport, then demonstrate <2% steady-state drops at the chosen capacity posture and loss parity against the existing EP implementation via `small_scale_abl_launch.py`.

h01 (cf 1.15 posture baseline) and h02 (latency-hiding scheduler + overlap limit 4, retesting the safe-flag retreat adopted on the broken barrier generation) are running. Queued: splits-per-peer sweep at EP64, command buffers at the #8277 capture set, XProf anatomy of the best configuration.

<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

Marin EP is an experimental Grug MoE backend for the GB200 hero: group-pooled waterfilling acceptance plus fused Mosaic-GPU transport, now working multi-process in the production 1-process/GPU topology. Upstream replaced NVSHMEM with the NCCL device API via collective metadata; with a patched PJRT wheel (kMaxPeers-128 + two 4096-alignment fixes), `--xla_gpu_enable_dynamic_slice_fusion=false`, and a separate collective allocator, the fused transport trains conformantly across nodes. The current EP64 hero best is 17.0 s/step, ~247k tokens/s/rack (~22.6% MFU) at 0.5-0.6% drops — from 18.1 s at the start of the campaign — via fused transport (17.75), Pallas Blackwell ragged-dot expert GEMMs (17.08, ~1.6x the QuACK/cuDNN path), and per-leg kernel configs (17.0). A correctness bug was found on the way: the cuDNN grouped Wgrad silently miscomputes unless group offsets are 64-aligned (#8339, fixed on the measurement branch). Profiles show the remaining 5 s to the 25% / 350k gate sits in attention/dense GEMMs, XLA fusion mass, and FSDP one-shot collectives rather than the MoE path.

### Helpful links
- Latest EP64 ladder + profile: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8311#issuecomment-5309381342 and https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8311#issuecomment-5309484707
- Multi-process transport unblock (three XLA findings + fixes): https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8311#issuecomment-5308550100
- Wgrad correctness bug: #8339; barrier-bound context: #8077, #8313, openxla/xla#47283
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description

Experimental fused expert-parallel MoE backend for `moe_hero_ep` (d6144, 192 latent experts, top-4, EP64 on GB200 NVL72), developed simulator-first against a dense oracle: behavior spec, NumPy oracle, message-passing correctness simulator with explicit backward, and L0/L1 performance models before hardware. The backend lives in `levanter.grug._moe.ep_marin` (+ `marin_ep_transport`); spec and research artifacts under `experiments/marin_ep/`. Branch `marin-ep`. This is an experimental backend: it has not run a full-scale training gate and is not a production default.

Differences from `fixed_all_to_all`/`ragged_all_to_all`:

- Acceptance is deterministic group-pooled waterfilling over global expert counts, pooling capacity across each owner's co-located experts. It is EP-degree invariant and drops 0.31% at cf 1.33 under hero-calibrated skew, vs ~4% for the per-cell rule at the same buffer bytes.
- Transport is one generic Mosaic-GPU put kernel (`put_segments`) that writes each owner's expert-major receive pool directly, eliminating both local permutes; dispatch and combine plans are transposes of each other, so the backward runs the same kernel with the opposite plan (custom_vjp).

## Hypothesis or Goal

Reach >= 25% MFU and >= 350k tokens/s/rack at the hero shape with EP64, keeping drops < 2% in the trained-router regime. Baseline `fixed_all_to_all`: 24.04% MFU, 262,683 tok/s at cf 1.30 with 3.96% drops.

## Status

- Multi-process fused transport validated end-to-end: 8-rank cross-node conformance (values, drops bit-identical to the ragged path, all gradients at the bf16 floor), then EP16 proxy (17.0 s vs 18.05 flat) and EP64 hero. Requires the patched PJRT wheel `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/research/mcwitt-ra2a/pjrt-kmax128-align4096-dev0811-20260816/` and `--xla_gpu_enable_dynamic_slice_fusion=false`; an upstream report of the three XLA findings is drafted pending review.
- EP64 hero ladder (25-step runs, same wheel/flags, single draws +/-2pp): brd 17.0 s/step (~247k tok/s, ~22.6% MFU, 0.5-0.6% drops) < mgpu-cute 17.75 < flat ragged 18.0. Flavors `ep-marin-mgpu-brd` / `ep-marin-mgpu-cudnn-cute` on branch `marin-ep-8081`.
- Expert GEMMs now run on jax's Pallas Blackwell ragged-dot kernel (fwd + dgrad; 1195-1531 TF/s per leg at true hero shapes, ~1.6x the QuACK/cuDNN path) with the 64-alignment-fixed cuDNN grouped wgrad (#8339). Hero dims need N-padding to the collective tile (2I=6272, I=3136).
- Dead ends recorded: PGLE OOMs on the fused flavor (its profiling pass falls back to dense a2a); command buffers neutral; scoped ragged groups and the hierarchical two-hop transport slower than flat; a memory-bound fused consumer hides only ~7% (M7a) — expert-major send order is the overlap lever, and M7b targets gating the ragged-dot group scheduler on arrival flags.
- Remaining gap to 25% MFU / 350k tok/s: ~5 s/step in attention/dense GEMMs (4.9 s busy), XLA fusions (3.5 s), and FSDP one-shot collectives (2.8 s + 1.05 s barriers) — outside the EP transport scope; fp8 wire + attention/fusion work are the ranked candidates.

## Links

* Logbook: `.agents/logbooks/marin-ep.md` (entries MEP-001..MEP-044; measurement branch `marin-ep-8081`, PR branch `marin-ep` / #8320)
* Plan: `.agents/projects/20260814_marin_ep_kernel.md`; M7 plan: `.agents/projects/marin-ep-m7.md`; spec: `experiments/marin_ep/SPEC.md`
* W&B: marin-community/marin_moe (runs `mep-*-20260815/16`)

## Decision Log

- 2026-08-14: adopted group-pooled waterfilling (pool group = experts per device) into the spec; per-cell and per-expert pooling both leave ~4% drops at cf 1.33.
- 2026-08-14: transport substrate = Pallas Mosaic-GPU remote puts + arrival semaphores (584 GB/s/device untuned on one tray, zero custom CUDA).
- 2026-08-15: multi-controller runs fall back to ragged transport after pinning the upstream NVSHMEM removal; hierarchical transport is the planned successor.

- 2026-08-16: multi-process fused transport adopted (collective metadata + patched wheel + dynamic-slice-fusion off) after the NVSHMEM-removal block proved obsolete; hierarchical transport retired.
- 2026-08-16: expert activation-path GEMMs moved to jax's Pallas Blackwell ragged-dot kernel; cuDNN grouped wgrad kept with the 64-alignment fix (#8339).

## Conclusion

issue.body:
Buffers that XLA assigns to the collective memory space can fail NCCL symmetric window registration (`ncclCommWindowRegister`). NCCL requires the window base address to be aligned to 4096 bytes (`NCCL_WIN_REQUIRED_ALIGNMENT`), but when collective memory is served by a separate BFC allocator, allocation bases are only 256-byte granular. The separate allocator is used with `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=cuda_async`, with `--xla_gpu_enable_allocator_spatial_partitioning=false`, or with `preallocate=false`. There is no flag workaround. The failure depends on BFC chunk placement, and two Mosaic-GPU collective kernels per executable make it deterministic for us.

## Context

We are porting an expert-parallel MoE dispatch/combine transport to a full training step, one process per GPU. The transport is a multi-process Pallas Mosaic-GPU kernel that writes peer buffers directly through `plgpu.remote_ref` and device semaphores. XLA therefore places the kernel's buffers in the collective memory space and registers them as NCCL windows. We use the separate-allocator configuration to work around an unrelated window-exhaustion problem with the default spatially partitioned pool, which we will file separately.

## Repro

Run a program with two multi-process Pallas Mosaic-GPU collective kernels per executable, on ≥ 2 processes with one process per GPU, with `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=cuda_async`. Our kernel and multi-process harness are public: [`put_segments`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/marin-ep-8081/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/marin_ep_transport.py) with the smoke [`smoke_mgpu_train_multiproc.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/marin-ep-8081/experiments/marin_ep/bench/smoke_mgpu_train_multiproc.py). The smoke's docstring lists the env vars. Four 1-GPU processes on one GB200 node suffice. We are happy to reduce this to a standalone script.

### Actual

Registration of the second kernel's buffers fails:

```
dev_runtime.cc:881 (ncclDevrWindowRegisterInGroup) NCCL WARN Window address must be suitably aligned.
INTERNAL: NCCL operation nccl_status failed: invalid argument
```

`TF_CPP_VMODULE=nccl_symmetric_memory=3` shows the failing window at a 256-granular offset (for example `0x…300`) inside the collective memory region.

### Expected

Allocations in the collective memory space meet the alignment that NCCL window registration requires. The default spatially partitioned pool already guarantees this by aligning to the collective memory granularity (2 MiB).

## Root cause hypothesis

XLA registers one window per `BufferAllocation` base ([nccl_symmetric_memory.cc#L88-L92](https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/60f8069e8b/xla/backends/gpu/collectives/nccl_symmetric_memory.cc#L88-L92)). When the default BFC pool serves collective memory via spatial partitioning, the allocator entry sets `min_alignment` to the collective memory granularity ([se_gpu_pjrt_client.cc#L1472-L1489](https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/60f8069e8b/xla/pjrt/gpu/se_gpu_pjrt_client.cc#L1472-L1489)). The `CreateCollectiveBFCAllocator` entry [sets no `min_alignment`](https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/60f8069e8b/xla/pjrt/gpu/se_gpu_pjrt_client.cc#L1579-L1592). PR #44156 removed an earlier size-rounding for collective buffers, on the premise that allocators configure per-memory-space alignment. This allocator entry never did.

## Fix validation

We rebuilt `jax-cuda13-pjrt` at jax `8d1be7d7` / xla `60f8069e` with one change: `BFCAllocator::RoundedBytes` rounds request sizes to 4096. The failure is gone at 8 ranks (2 nodes) and at 64 ranks (one NVL72 rack, 25/25 training steps, outputs numerically conformant against a reference path). The rounding is a blunt instrument. Setting `min_alignment` on the allocator entry looks like the intended mechanism, but we validated only the rounding variant. Also observed: raising `kMinAllocationBits` to 12 instead trips the `BinForSize(bin_size) == BinFromIndex(b)` construction invariant.

## Environment

- GB200 NVL72, CUDA 13. The failure reproduces on one node with 4 GPUs, one process per GPU.
- jax/jaxlib/plugin/pjrt `0.11.1.dev20260809` and `.dev20260816` nightlies, NCCL 2.30.7
- Analyzed at xla `60f8069e8b`. The code paths above are unchanged at `f0bfd165e0` (2026-08-17).
- Related: #47283 (`kMaxPeers` bound in the multi-GPU barrier kernel, same campaign). Two further issues affect Mosaic-GPU collective kernels but have flag workarounds: window registrations exhaust NCCL's per-rank window space under the default allocator configuration, and dynamic-slice fusion drops the collective memory space from buffers of fused kernels. We will file both separately.

issue.body:
When a Mosaic-GPU collective kernel consumes a slice of another op's output, `DynamicSliceFusionRewriterV2` wraps the kernel and the slice into a fusion. The fusion boundary then prevents the collective-memory coloring from selecting the kernel's operands and results, so its buffers are allocated in default memory and NCCL symmetric window registration fails at the first execution.

Context: we hit this while porting a multi-process expert-parallel MoE transport (Pallas Mosaic-GPU kernels that write peer buffers through `plgpu.remote_ref`) to a full training step. It supersedes #47406: the failures we first attributed to allocator alignment are produced by this pass.

## Minimal repro

Verified on GB200 (4 processes × 1 GPU, one node, stock nightly `0.11.1.dev20260809`): with default flags, every process fails. With `--xla_gpu_enable_dynamic_slice_fusion=false`, every process prints ok. The first kernel runs unfused and works. The second kernel consumes `(y1 @ w)[:15]` and fails.

```bash
# failing arm (default flags), one process per GPU
for i in 0 1 2 3; do
  XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=cuda_async CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$i \
    python repro.py 127.0.0.1:9991 4 $i > /tmp/repro_fail_$i.log 2>&1 &
done; wait
# workaround arm
for i in 0 1 2 3; do
  XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=cuda_async CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$i \
  XLA_FLAGS=--xla_gpu_enable_dynamic_slice_fusion=false \
    python repro.py 127.0.0.1:9992 4 $i > /tmp/repro_ok_$i.log 2>&1 &
done; wait
```

<details>
<summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
# python repro.py <coordinator_host:port> <num_processes> <process_id>  # 1 process/GPU
import sys

import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpy as np
from jax import lax
from jax.experimental import pallas as pl
from jax.experimental.pallas import mosaic_gpu as plgpu
from jax.sharding import AxisType, Mesh
from jax.sharding import PartitionSpec as P

coord, n_proc, pid = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), int(sys.argv[3])
jax.distributed.initialize(coord, num_processes=n_proc, process_id=pid)
n = jax.device_count()
mesh = Mesh(np.array(jax.devices()), ("x",), axis_types=(AxisType.Explicit,))


def ring_shift(x):
    """Every device writes its block into the right neighbor's output."""

    def body(x_ref, out_ref):
        sem = pl.get_global(plgpu.SemaphoreType.REGULAR)
        dev = lax.axis_index("x")
        right = lax.rem(dev + 1, lax.axis_size("x"))
        dst = plgpu.remote_ref(out_ref, {"x": right})

        def scoped(smem, barrier):
            plgpu.copy_gmem_to_smem(x_ref, smem, barrier)
            plgpu.barrier_wait(barrier)
            plgpu.copy_smem_to_gmem(smem, dst)
            plgpu.wait_smem_to_gmem(0, wait_read_only=False)

        pl.run_scoped(scoped, plgpu.SMEM(x_ref.shape, x_ref.dtype), plgpu.Barrier(num_arrivals=1),
                      collective_axes="wg")
        pl.semaphore_signal(sem, device_id={"x": right})
        pl.semaphore_wait(sem, value=1)

    return plgpu.kernel(body, grid=(1,), grid_names=("sm",), num_threads=1, thread_name="wg",
                        out_shape=jax.ShapeDtypeStruct(x.shape, x.dtype))(x)


def f():
    dev = lax.axis_index("x").astype(jnp.float32)
    a = jnp.full((19, 256), dev, jnp.float32)
    y1 = ring_shift(a)
    # The second collective kernel consumes a static slice of a GEMM output.
    # The dynamic-slice fusion pass wraps the kernel and the slice into a
    # fusion, and the coloring no longer selects the kernel's buffers.
    w = jnp.full((256, 256), 0.01, jnp.float32)
    b = (y1 @ w)[:15]
    y2 = ring_shift(b)
    return y1, y2


run = jax.jit(jax.shard_map(f, mesh=mesh, in_specs=(), out_specs=(P("x"), P("x"))))
y1, y2 = jax.block_until_ready(run())
left = float((jax.process_index() - 1) % n)  # 1 process per GPU: global device rank == process index
left2 = float((jax.process_index() - 2) % n)
np.testing.assert_array_equal(np.asarray(y1.addressable_shards[0].data)[0, :4], np.full(4, left, np.float32))
np.testing.assert_allclose(np.asarray(y2.addressable_shards[0].data)[0, :4], np.full(4, left2 * 2.56, np.float32), rtol=1e-3)
print(f"process {jax.process_index()}: ok ({n} devices)", flush=True)
```

</details>

### Actual

Every process fails at the first execution:

```
jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError: INTERNAL: NCCL operation nccl_status failed: unhandled cuda error ... 'Cuda failure 1 'invalid argument''. [executable_name='jit_f']
```

`TF_CPP_VMODULE=nccl_symmetric_memory=3,collective_memory=3` identifies the failing registration. The collective arena registers fine, then registration is requested for the GEMM output allocation that passed through the fusion boundary — a default-memory (cudaMallocAsync pool) pointer:

```
nccl_symmetric_memory.cc:85] Create NCCL symmetric memory on comm=... from: ptr=0xf199f4a00000; size=2097152
collective_memory.cc:560] [0]  Acquire collective memory for global device id 0: run_id=... symmetric=1 multicast=0 peer=0
nccl_symmetric_memory.cc:85] Create NCCL symmetric memory on comm=... from: ptr=0x340000000; size=19456
→ Cuda failure 1 'invalid argument'
```

(19456 bytes = the full `f32[19,256]` GEMM output; the fusion operand is the whole producer buffer, sliced inside the fusion. With a BFC default arena instead of cudaMallocAsync, the same escape surfaces as `Window address must be suitably aligned`.)

The after-optimizations HLO shows the mechanism. With default flags, the second kernel sits inside the fusion and no operand or result carries `S(1)`:

```
%dynamic-slice-fusion (p0: f32[19,256], p1: s32[1]) -> (f32[15,256], s32[1]) {
  ...
  ROOT %mpmd_map.16 = (f32[15,256]{1,0}, s32[1]{0}) custom-call(%slice.4, %p1), custom_call_target="mosaic_gpu_v2", ...
}
...
%dynamic_slice_fusion = (f32[15,256]{1,0}, s32[1]{0}) fusion(%gemm_fusion_dot_general.3, %copy.8), kind=kCustom, calls=%dynamic-slice-fusion, ...
```

while the unfused first kernel in the same module is fully colored (`%loop_broadcast_fusion = f32[19,256]{1,0:S(1)}` feeding `%mpmd_map.14`). With the flag off, both call results are colored:

```
%mpmd_map.14 = (f32[19,256]{1,0:S(1)}, s32[1]{0:S(1)}) custom-call(...), custom_call_target="mosaic_gpu_v2", ...
%mpmd_map.15 = (f32[15,256]{1,0:S(1)}, s32[1]{0:S(1)}) custom-call(%wrapped_slice, ...), custom_call_target="mosaic_gpu_v2", ...
```

### Expected

Fusing a collective custom call does not change the memory space of its operands and results, or the rewriter does not wrap such calls.

## Root cause hypothesis

The rewriter's [predicate](https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/60f8069e8b/xla/service/gpu/gpu_compiler.cc#L1649-L1678) accepts any registered typed-FFI custom call, with no exclusion for calls that need collective memory. The collective coloring and copy-insertion analyses (for example [IsMosaicWithMultimem](https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/60f8069e8b/xla/service/gpu/ir_emission_utils.cc#L166-L171) and its callers) do not look through the fusion boundary, and the fusion instruction carries neither the custom-call opcode nor the hero's backend config. At execution, JAX's Mosaic-GPU FFI prepare handler ([`MosaicGpuPrepare`](https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/blob/8d1be7d7/jaxlib/mosaic/gpu/custom_call.cc)) requests symmetric registration of the resulting default-memory buffer, which fails as shown above. The pass is default-on since PR #43831 (2026-06-30).

## Workaround

`--xla_gpu_enable_dynamic_slice_fusion=false`. Validated at 4, 8, and 64 ranks; no measurable performance cost on our workload.

## Environment

- GB200 NVL72, one node, one process per GPU. CUDA 13, driver 595.71.05, NCCL 2.30.7.
- `jax`, `jaxlib`, `jax-cuda13-plugin`, `jax-cuda13-pjrt` `0.11.1.dev20260809` (stock nightlies from the jax-public-nightly registry); also reproduced on `.dev20260816`.
- Analyzed at xla `60f8069e8b`. The code paths are unchanged at `f0bfd165e0` (2026-08-17).
- Related: #47283. Supersedes #47406.

issue.body:
Reference implementation: https://github.com/cursor/mixture-of-kittens

## TL;DR — 2026-08-13

The supported `mok_like` path is ready for review and production extraction at the tested configuration. Confidence is high for numerical correctness, optimizer-state evolution, strict zero-drop routing, normal execution through two racks, and bounded propagation of synchronous native-handler failures. The final 32-process/128-GB200 run completed 100 updates with exact runtime audits and 83.77% weak-scale efficiency.

- Stable branch: [`codex/upstream-mok-like`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/codex/upstream-mok-like)
- Snapshot tag: [`mok-like-v15-two-rack-2026-08-12`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/mok-like-v15-two-rack-2026-08-12)
- Commit: [`bceba3c7814f45f556109f202386f85c12844527`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/bceba3c7814f45f556109f202386f85c12844527)
- Final two-rack run: [W&B](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mok-scale-012-v15-dropless-2rack-host176-100-20260812-1632) · [XProf](https://iris.oa.dev/proxy/xprof/open?uri=s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Ftmp%2Fttl%3D30d%2Fxprof%2Fmok-scale-012-v15-dropless-2rack-host176-100-20260812-1632)
- Detailed record: [barrier-free/zero-copy/scale logbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/mok-like-v15-two-rack-2026-08-12/.agents/logbooks/8108-mok-like-barrier-free.md) · [earlier implementation logbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/mok-like-v15-two-rack-2026-08-12/.agents/logbooks/8108-mixture-of-kittens-consolidation.md)
- Failure incident: [Echo wiki 137](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/137)

One combined property is unproven: cancellation while a healthy sibling invocation is simultaneously resident in the other workspace slot. Healthy two-slot overlap and one-failure/one-success isolation pass separately. Asynchronous CUDA context corruption remains process-terminal by design.

## Supported configuration

The sealed path uses:

- L48, width 6,144, E8/top-4, intermediate width 3,072, BF16 compute;
- one JAX process per four local GB200s, process-local EP4, and data parallelism across processes;
- strict schedule capacity factor 4, with zero dropped assignments in every sealed run;
- XLA-owned peer-visible forward inputs and staged backward peer storage;
- one native workspace slot;
- shared eager `cuda_async`, device-memory fraction 0.80, and no manual pool trims;
- a 176 GiB process-global pinned-host arena under a 900 GiB pod-memory request;
- local-only XLA per-fusion autotune cache;
- zero child retries, preemption retries, or tolerated task failures.

The launcher preset is still named `promoted_dropless_v12`; the native FFI schema in the tagged source is v15. Use the tag or commit, not the preset name, as native-version provenance.

## Confidence

| Area | Confidence | Evidence | Limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Healthy numerical training | High | Full forward/VJP comparisons, route extremes, dependent calls, concurrent calls, and 64 sequential momentum updates against an independent reference | Tested model shape, BF16 path, and optimizer sequence; not every possible model shape or dtype |
| Strict dropless routing | High | Capacity-factor-4 runs completed with exact zero dropped assignments on 4, 8, 64, and 128 GB200s | The guarantee depends on the supported factor-4 schedule and four-way local expert parallelism |
| Runtime protocol and slot reuse | High | Exact forward/backward handler counts, generation checks, slot audits, and zero protocol anomalies through 100 updates on 32 processes | Normal path uses one slot; two-slot reuse is covered by targeted correctness gates rather than the final training run |
| Synchronous failure closure | High within scope | Four isolated forward/backward failure points closed in under one second on four GB200s; a process-zero backward failure became the same error on both JAX processes in about 3.23 seconds and both tasks exited cleanly | Requires a usable independent cancellation stream; asynchronous sticky CUDA failures are terminal |
| Failure isolation with concurrent RunIds | Medium-high | One injected failure and one numerically correct success completed without generation or reuse anomalies | The short failure gates serialized before slot overlap; simultaneous failed/healthy residency is not proven |
| One-rack and two-rack execution | High for the tested shape | 16-process/64-GB200 and 32-process/128-GB200 gates completed with finite losses, zero drops, exact all-process audits, and clean Iris exits | Does not prove different expert group sizes, more than two racks, or much longer training horizons |
| Throughput | Medium-high | Matched two-node v15/v12 pair, one-rack v15/v12 pair, and a 100-step two-rack v15 seal | Two-rack v12 runs showed fabric-related variance; one successful v15 long run does not eliminate cluster variance |
| Host-memory margin | High for 900 GiB pods | 176 GiB arena passed one node, one rack, and two racks; the final run retained 106.5 GiB cgroup headroom with zero memory events | Do not reduce the 900 GiB pod request without a separate full-rack cgroup gate |

## Final results

### Numerical and stateful parity

The 64-step stateful gate alternated balanced, zero-token, skewed, and all-to-one routes while applying sequential momentum updates. Outputs, losses, all gradients, parameters, and optimizer state stayed within the configured numerical tolerances. Drops and inactive-expert gradients were exactly zero. The run completed 256 forward and 256 backward handlers, used slot zero only, and reported zero generation or reuse anomalies.

The broader correctness matrix also covered balanced and adversarial routing, 1/2/8/32-macrobatch schedules, offloaded saved context, dependent back-to-back VJPs, concurrent executions, corrupt saved-context stamps, and strict all-to-one capacity.

### Failure closure

V15 returns a scalar failure status from native forward/backward calls. Generation- and slot-scoped device cancellation releases the local EP4 peer group. A `lax.pmax` over non-expert mesh axes makes the failure decision uniform before later shared-weight collectives. Those collectives execute only in the success branch; the failure branch raises through a pure typed-FFI fence.

This structure came from two failures in earlier candidates:

1. Device-only cancellation let healthy ranks leave the FFI and enter later `lax.psum` calls after another rank failed. The distributed job then hung.
2. Uniform failure propagation initially left backward registered as an ordered side effect. JAX retained the expected failure in its runtime token and raised it again during `effects_barrier()` at interpreter shutdown.

Making backward destination-passing and pure removed the retained ordered token. The negative distributed harness closes the native runtime and calls `jax.distributed.shutdown()` explicitly after checking the uniform error.

The accepted two-process gate injected a backward failure on process zero before input readiness. Both processes observed the same phase-neutral error in 3.2309 and 3.2367 seconds. Each reported four forward and four backward handlers, `[2, 0]` slot acquisitions on every local rank, maximum active slots one, and zero generation or reuse anomalies. Both Iris tasks exited zero.

### Performance and scale

| Run | Devices | Window | Total tok/s | Tok/s/GPU | Weak-scale efficiency | Result |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| V12 matched baseline | 8 | 60–79 | 38,632.67 | 4,829.08 | 93.48% against four-GPU dropless baseline | Pass |
| V15 matched candidate | 8 | 60–79 | 40,110.63 | 5,013.83 | 97.05% against the same baseline | Pass; +3.83% vs v12 pair |
| V12 host-176 one-rack | 64 | 10–24 | 314,110.12 | 4,907.97 | 95.00% | Pass |
| V15 host-176 one-rack | 64 | 10–24 | 309,026.65 | 4,828.54 | 93.47% | Pass; −1.62% vs v12 pair |
| V12 long two-rack | 128 | 60–79 | 516,415.19 | 4,034.49 | 78.10% | Correctness pass; performance gate miss |
| V15 long two-rack | 128 | 60–79 | 553,963.07 | 4,327.84 | 83.77% | Pass; +7.27% vs long v12 run |

The final v15 two-rack run used exactly two hard NVLink domains with 16 nodes each. All 32 tasks completed 100 finite zero-drop rows. Every process reported 19,200 forward and 19,200 backward handlers, zero forward staging, exactly 76,800 staged-backward calls and 30,964,029,849,600 staged bytes, slot one unused, maximum active slots one, and zero protocol, generation, reuse, trim, or slot anomalies.

The matched two-node pair showed no measurable scalar failure-agreement overhead; the v15 arm was faster in that pair. Process-zero HBM was 5.73 GiB higher in the v15 W&B sample than in the v12 baseline, but both runs completed without device-memory errors. The source of the sampled HBM difference is unresolved.

### Host memory

The original 192 GiB pinned-host arena left little margin under a 900 GiB pod. Direct cgroup and `smaps` measurements showed that the approximately 816 GiB peak was real process-private anonymous memory, not double-counted descendants.

- A 128 GiB arena failed before step zero when each host BFC allocator attempted a 99 GiB allocation.
- A 176 GiB arena passed 25 steps and reduced the one-node cgroup peak by 70.18 GiB relative to the 192 GiB control without a throughput regression.
- The v15 one-rack run peaked at 805.90 GiB, leaving 94.10 GiB of cgroup headroom.
- The final v15 two-rack run peaked at 793.49 GiB on process zero, leaving 106.51 GiB of cgroup headroom. All memory-event counters stayed zero.

The promoted arena is 176 GiB. The pod request remains 900 GiB.

## What was tried and rejected

### Communication and staging

- Global peer barriers worked but cost throughput. Generation-tagged producer readiness and destination completion replaced them.
- XLA one-shot symmetric copying was correct but roughly an order of magnitude too slow.
- Device-initiated ragged transfer improved the first implementation but remained slower than the fused path.
- Forward zero-copy improved the staged control by about 0.5% in the matched four-GB200 comparison and is promoted.
- Full backward zero-copy was numerically correct but 2.40% slower than staged backward. Hybrid variants recovered most of the loss but did not beat forward-only zero-copy. Staged backward is promoted.

### Capacity and routed-weight gradients

- Schedule factor 1.1 was fast but not dropless; the sealed 100-step control dropped about 0.15% of assignments in the scored window.
- The original capacity-dependent routed-weight-gradient result made strict factor-4 graphs too large.
- One canonical FP32 routed-weight-gradient result per local expert removed that capacity-dependent XLA reduction. Factor 4 then completed route extremes and full-model scale gates with exact zero drops.

### Device allocation

- Shared eager `cuda_async` at fraction 0.85 repeatedly failed on the same 132,687,700,848-byte temporary near update 66.
- Raising the fraction, using one workspace slot, synchronizing results, VMM, recurring manual trims, and parallel trim did not remove the deterministic failure.
- V12 telemetry showed that trim returned physical backing exactly, graph-pool memory was zero, and bytes outside the default pool stayed constant. The failure was tight default-pool large-allocation reuse, not a graph-memory or external-allocation leak.
- A separate temp pool and shared on-demand allocation completed but cost about 17% throughput.
- Shared eager allocation at fraction 0.80 crossed update 66 and completed 100 steps without trims. This is the promoted setting.

### Failure-control tests

- Blocking a host callback until a second invocation leased a slot caused a five-minute circular wait because PJRT could not dispatch the second callback on that occupied lane.
- A nonblocking lease-count hook could miss the injection when both callbacks observed insufficient overlap.
- Injecting on the second distinct invocation key produced one expected failure and one correct success, but the short calls serialized through slot zero. Compiling separate static call sites also serialized.
- A correct combined overlap proof requires a test-only, generation-safe device witness. The witness must observe both invocations resident without blocking a host callback. It is not part of the stable implementation.

## Unproven and out of scope

1. Cancellation while a healthy sibling is concurrently resident in the other workspace slot is not proven in one gate. Healthy same-executable two-slot overlap and one-failure/one-success isolation are proven separately.
2. Asynchronous illegal-address faults or sticky CUDA context corruption do not have bounded in-process recovery. The process must terminate and be replaced by the job supervisor.
3. More than two racks, local expert groups larger than four GPUs, other model shapes, other dtypes, and runs longer than 100 optimizer updates have not been sealed.
4. Full backward zero-copy remains an optimization target. It is not the supported configuration because the measured path was slower.
5. Cross-rack throughput varies with the fabric. The final v15 run passed 80%, but an earlier v12 run reached only 78.10% with a wide step-time tail and no numerical or protocol failure.
6. The 5.73 GiB process-zero HBM difference in the matched v15/v12 pair is not attributed.
7. The branch is a reproducible research snapshot, not yet merged into the repository default branch.

## Decision log

- 2026-08-10: remove global peer barriers; use generation-tagged readiness and completion.
- 2026-08-11: promote forward zero-copy and staged backward; reject full backward zero-copy on throughput.
- 2026-08-11: use canonical FP32 routed-weight gradients and schedule factor 4 for strict zero-drop routing.
- 2026-08-11: use shared eager `cuda_async` at fraction 0.80; reject manual trim and on-demand/separate-pool paths.
- 2026-08-12: propagate synchronous failures as device data before later collectives; make backward pure destination-passing FFI.
- 2026-08-12: promote the 176 GiB pinned-host arena while retaining the 900 GiB pod request.
- 2026-08-12: advance v15 after matched two-node, one-rack, and two-rack gates passed.

## Handoff

The tagged v15 snapshot is the stable implementation for the supported configuration. The next repository change should extract it into a reviewable PR without changing the sealed runtime or launcher defaults. Review should focus on the failure-status dataflow, pure backward FFI contract, generated native wait/cancellation code, pinned-host preset, and exact all-process audit schema.

Do not block adoption on the combined failed/healthy overlap witness unless that property is a production requirement. If it is required, build the witness on a confidence branch and retain the strict acceptance condition: both workspace slots active, one expected failure, one numerically correct success, exact per-slot counters, and zero generation or reuse anomalies.

Keep the issue open until the stable snapshot is merged or an explicit decision is made to retain it as an experiment-only branch.

issue.body:
Add `marin_ep`, an expert-parallel MoE backend for Grug that replaces the incumbent
`fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all` path on the EP64 hero, and pin `moe_hero_ep` to it.

Two things change relative to the incumbent. The drop rule becomes group-pooled
waterfilling: one global accept decision taken before dispatch from an all-gathered
per-expert count vector, giving each expert its `min(count, capacity)` floor and
handing the leftover slack to the overflowing experts by capped cumsum. The incumbent
instead drops twice — once against a sender-side per-destination wire pool, again
against a receiver-side per-expert cap — so a token can survive routing and still die
on the wire. Transport becomes a persistent Mosaic-GPU kernel that issues the dispatch
puts and runs the arrival-gated gate/up GEMM in the same kernel, so the exchange never
appears as a separate collective; the down GEMM runs on the Pallas Blackwell grouped
GEMM and the weight gradients on cuDNN grouped Wgrad.

Measured on the EP64 GB200 hero at main's exact config (d6144, 48 layers, E384 × 3072
top-8, b1024 × 4096), two draws per arm, 25 steps each: the incumbent runs 16.9–17.0
s/it at 1.0–2.4% final drops; `marin_ep` at capacity factor 1.05 runs 17.5 s/it at
0.67–0.80%. Training loss matches to 6.07–6.10 across all arms. Dropping the capacity
factor to 1.0 recovers 0.2 s/it but returns drops to the incumbent's level, so 1.05 is
the operating point.

The 3.4% throughput deficit is real and replicated, and it is not a scheduling
problem: total device busy time is equal on both sides (~18.6 vs ~18.7 s/step). The
incumbent spends ~2.9 s/step in all-to-all kernels and hides ~2 s of it behind
compute, while the fused transport has nothing left to overlap, so its busy time is
its wall time. Closing the gap needs kernel work inside the fused transport, not
tuning: an 8-point sweep found the shipped stage/lane/chunk constants optimal within
±1.7%.

The hero run pins a JAX nightly and a patched `jax-cuda13-pjrt` wheel. The stock
multi-GPU barrier kernel caps `kMaxPeers` at 32, overflows its signal region at 64
ranks, and kills step 0 with an illegal address; the patch raises the cap to 128
(openxla/xla#47283) and adds 4096-byte buffer-assignment alignment for NCCL window
registration. Both are install-time substitutions in the task setup script, not
repository changes.

Part of #8311

issue.body:
Reworks the ragged all-to-all expert-parallel MoE backend into a replacement for the pooled-wave hero transport. In an A/B at the hero shape — both arms restored from the live hero's step-6000 checkpoint on real data, one NVL72 rack, transport the only variable — ragged delivers:

- **matching-to-slightly-ahead throughput**: **22.87 vs 22.71 MFU**, with the two arms run back to back on the same rack so placement differences cannot account for the gap (standard deviation across the scored steps: 0.11 for ragged, 0.59 for pooled-wave; three earlier runs of the ragged configuration ranged 22.34–22.58)
- **~150× lower drop rate**: **0.018%** vs 2.67% of expert assignments under the trained router, with the loss at the scored step correspondingly lower (1.4727 vs 1.4777)
- **~12 GiB lower runtime device peak**: **137.9 vs 149.9 GiB** at identical steady-state footprint

This PR does not change the default backend: the `moe_hero_ep` entry points keep `fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all`, and the ragged backend is opt-in via `moe_implementation="ragged_all_to_all"`.

Key changes:

- **Expert-granular transport data path** — one `ragged_all_to_all` update per (peer, local expert): senders read each expert group's accepted prefix in place and rows arrive grouped by expert, replacing ~1.1 s/step of repeat/sort/compact permutes. With chunking, **+1.5 MFU** over the prior ragged path.
- **Sequential expert chunks** — local experts run in two chunks with per-chunk capacity, halving the transport buffers XLA cannot rematerialize. Not a tuning choice: the unchunked graph needs 192–194 GiB against 184 GiB HBM and OOMs at the first hero step.
- **QuACK SM100 grouped GEMMs + cuDNN grouped weight gradients** for the expert MLP — the core of the earlier **16.1% → 21.9%** stack. Those two figures were measured before the current protocol and are not directly comparable to the numbers above. SM100 + SiLU only; everything else keeps XLA's `ragged_dot`.
- **Device-initiated transport** — the ragged backend engages XLA's device-initiated (NCCL LSA) ragged-all-to-all kernel through `XLA_FLAGS` defaults it sets itself. The kernel partitions copy work across CTAs by bytes, so splitting a peer transfer into several updates buys no load balance and only adds granularity cost (21.12 MFU when we measured it at 64 splits, against 22.34–22.58 unsplit). The backend therefore exposes no splitting option, and the two flags are not overridable: the host-launched kernel would need both flags cleared together plus the update splitting this backend does not produce, so a partial override would silently run a configuration nothing here measures.
- **Fused combine gather + weighted sum** and a backend-specific scheduling posture (latency-hiding scheduler off, collective overlap 1) — part of the stack above. The scheduler is off for memory, not scheduling: its longer live ranges fail NCCL's first-step allocations at the current HBM budget, and a follow-up that offloads layer activations to pinned host re-enables it at a measured gain (#8317).
- **`--master-params` option** — fp32 weights on device instead of a pinned-host master: **~+0.4 MFU**.
- **Validation harness** — the 4-GPU `ragged_ep_check` gates forward and gradients against an exact fp32 dense reference, both at a capacity high enough that nothing is clipped and in the drop regime the hero actually trains in. For the latter it computes which assignments survive in NumPy — accepted rows are the prefix of each expert group under a greedy first-sender-wins gate, so the surviving set is a pure function of the routing and the capacity — and requires the transport to equal dense over exactly the rows it kept. It also records which kernels the run selected, since that depends on the device and the installed packages. Nothing runs it on a schedule, and it sits under `experiments/` rather than `tests/cluster/`, because the repository has no marker, fixture, or workflow for a test that needs particular accelerators (#8704). That same gap silences the two unit tests that exercise this backend end to end: both skip under CI's single CPU device, and `addopts` carries no `-rs`, so the skips do not appear in the output. Separately, a d768 ablation pair (10.8k steps, identical settings) has ragged ahead of pooled-wave on train loss (**1.939 vs 1.956**), eval bpb (**0.975 vs 1.033**), and steady-state drop rate (**~0.03% vs ~2.7%** at that scale).

Context: pooled-wave is the hero default but drops a low-single-digit percentage of expert assignments at steady state. The goal here is at-least-parity throughput with materially fewer drops, without touching the model or precision. That trade matters most for long-context training, where a batch holds fewer, longer examples: per-shard token pools average over fewer documents, routing skew grows, and capacity clipping bites harder. Memory is a second operational motivation. The hero's intermittent OOMs traced to the step peak overshooting the cuda_async release threshold (#8490), and main now holds the production pooled-wave hero under that threshold by shrinking the train-step arena (#8507, slop factor 85) with the master kept on pinned host. Ragged reaches the same safety with ~12 GiB to spare: in that same paired run, where both arms carry the heavier fp32-on-device master, pooled-wave still peaks 11.7 GiB over the threshold (149.9 vs 138.2 GiB) while ragged sits just under it (137.9 GiB) — headroom that loosens the arena and master-placement constraints the pooled posture needs.

Caveat — **quoted throughput depends on an XLA patch, shipped separately.** The device kernel itself runs on stock XLA (jax ≥ 0.11.1 defines the flags; older jaxlibs abort at import on unknown `XLA_FLAGS` entries), but its stock CTA assignment starves under trained-router skew and measures ~19.4% MFU at this shape. The quoted numbers use a one-commit balanced-CTA-assignment patch, [mcwitt/xla@d6d3132a90](https://github.com/mcwitt/xla/commit/d6d3132a90dada14d570b66da38eccb7f6d774a3) (2.35× on the standalone transport benchmark; being upstreamed). This PR does not ship a wheel; the pinned build lands in a follow-up. The 4-GPU validation has been run green on GB200 against the host-launched kernel, which exercises the expert-MLP kernels and the offset arithmetic; re-running it against the device kernel needs that build.

Part of #8317. Per-arm ledgers and trace anatomy live on `research/mcwitt/8317-ragged-tune` under `autoresearch/loop-260821-leg2/` (one-shot tuning) and on `research/mcwitt/8317-dk-native` under `autoresearch/loop-260824-dkperf/` (device-kernel root-cause and the balanced-CTA result).

📝 Summary of Changes
- Add kNumThreads = 32 (launch size) separate from kMaxPeers (peer capacity), and raise kMaxPeers to 128.
- Make SyncRemoteBlocks loop over peers with a blockDim.x stride so one warp can synchronize with any number of peers up to kMaxPeers.
- Launch both barrier kernels with ThreadDim(kNumThreads, 1, 1) and add the missing peer-count check to LaunchMultiGpuBarrierWithNccl.

🎯 Justification
- Fixes the >32-GPU crash in https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/47283.
- Simply raising kMaxPeers to 128 would launch 4 warps and race on the sync_counter read/write in SyncRemoteBlocksAndUpdateCounter. Keeping the launch to one warp avoids the race by construction.
- No behavior change at ≤32 peers.
